forms: I am / you are / he, she, it is / we, you, they are
Negative: I am not, he is not (isn't), they are not (aren't)
Question: Am I ...? Are you ...? Is she ...?

mistakes.note: With she, he and it we use is.

forms: a + a consonant sound: a book
an + a vowel sound: an apple, an hour
the - a particular thing, or one already mentioned

examples.text: I have a dog. The dog is big.

mistakes.note: A job in the singular needs an article.

forms: Usually -s: book - books
After s, x, ch, sh: -es: box - boxes
Consonant + y becomes -ies: city - cities
Irregular: man - men, child - children, person - people

mistakes.note: The plural of child is irregular.

forms: this / these - near; that / those - far
my, your, his, her, its, our, their + noun
's shows who owns something: Tom's bag

mistakes.note: For the plural we need these.

forms: I / you / we / they + verb: I work
he / she / it + verb-s: she works
Time words: always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day

mistakes.note: With he, she and it, the Present Simple takes -s.

forms: Negative: do not (don't) / does not (doesn't) + verb
Question: Do you ...? Does he ...?
After does, the verb has no -s

mistakes.note: After does, the verb has no -s.

forms: There is + singular: There is a bed
There are + plural: There are two windows
Negative: isn't / aren't (any)
Question: Is there ...? Are there any ...?

examples.text: There is a bank near here.
Is there a park in your town?

mistakes.note: For the plural we need there are.

forms: can + verb without to: I can swim
Negative: can't (cannot)
Question: Can you help me?

mistakes.note: We do not use to after can.

forms: I / you / we / they have got; he / she / it has got
Negative: haven't / hasn't got
Question: Have you got ...? Has she got ...?

mistakes.note: With she, he and it we need has.

forms: Place: in (inside), on (on a surface), at (at a point)
Time: at 5 o'clock, on Monday, in July
More: next to, under, behind, between

examples.text: The keys are on the table.

mistakes.note: With days of the week we use on.

forms: V + -ed: worked, played
Verbs ending in -e add -d: live - lived
Consonant + y becomes -ied: study - studied
Doubling: stop - stopped

mistakes.note: A consonant + y becomes -ied.

forms: go - went, see - saw, have - had, make - made, take - took
to be: I / he / she / it was; you / we / they were
Negative and question: did + base form

mistakes.note: Go is an irregular verb, and its past form is went.

forms: Negative: did not (didn't) + verb
Question: Did you ...? What did she ...?
After did, the verb is in the base form

mistakes.note: After did, the verb is in the base form.

forms: am / is / are + verb-ing: I am working
Negative: am not / isn't / aren't + -ing
Question: Are you listening?

examples.text: I'm staying with a friend this week.

mistakes.note: State verbs (know, like, want) are usually not used in the Continuous.

forms: Present Simple: habits, timetables, permanent facts
Present Continuous: now or temporary
Clues: always, every day / now, at the moment, today

examples.text: She works in a bank, but today she's working at home.

mistakes.note: An action at the moment of speaking needs the Present Continuous.

forms: am / is / are + going to + verb
Negative: I'm not going to ...
Question: Are you going to ...?

examples.text: I'm going to visit my aunt on Sunday.
Look at the clouds! It's going to rain.
Are you going to study tonight?

mistakes.wrong: I going to buy a car.
mistakes.right: I'm going to buy a car.
mistakes.note: You need the verb to be: am, is or are.

forms: will + verb: I will call you
Negative: won't (will not)
Question: Will you help me?

examples.text: I promise I won't be late.

mistakes.note: We do not use to after will.

forms: Short adjectives: -er / the -est: tall - taller - the tallest
Long adjectives: more / the most: more interesting
Irregular: good - better - best; bad - worse - worst
as ... as - equal

examples.text: My bag is cheaper than yours.
This is the most expensive hotel.
He is as tall as me.

mistakes.note: Short adjectives take -er, not more.

forms: Countable: many, a few, some, any
Uncountable: much, a little, some, any
a lot of - for both
some - in positive sentences; any - in questions and negatives

examples.text: How much water do you drink?

mistakes.note: Money is uncountable, so we use much.

forms: have to / must - it is necessary
don't have to - it is not necessary; mustn't - it is forbidden
should + verb - advice

examples.text: I have to get up early.

mistakes.wrong: You mustn't come if you don't want to.
mistakes.right: You don't have to come if you don't want to.
mistakes.note: Mustn't means it is forbidden; when it is not necessary, say don't have to.

forms: Manner: adjective + -ly: slow - slowly
Irregular: good - well, fast - fast, hard - hard
Frequency: before the verb, after to be: She always walks. He is never late.

examples.text: I usually get up at seven.

mistakes.note: A verb needs the adverb well, not the adjective good.

forms: have / has + V3: I have seen
Negative: haven't / hasn't + V3
Question: Have you ever ...?
for + a period, since + a starting point

examples.text: I have lived here for ten years.
She has never been to Italy.

mistakes.note: With yesterday we need the Past Simple.

forms: Past Simple: the time is named, the action is finished
Present Perfect: the result or the experience matters, the time is not named
Only the Past Simple: yesterday, last week, ago, in 2019

examples.text: I lost my keys. (I don't have them now.)

mistakes.note: A question about when something happened is in the Past Simple.

forms: was / were + verb-ing
Background: Past Continuous; event: Past Simple
while - a long action; when - a short one

examples.text: I was walking home when it started to rain.
While she was reading, he was cooking.

mistakes.note: After was and were we need the -ing form.

forms: If + Present Simple, will + verb
Not possible: If you will come
unless = if not

examples.text: If it rains, we will stay at home.
I'll call you if I have time.
Unless you hurry, you'll be late.

mistakes.wrong: If it will rain, we stay at home.
mistakes.right: If it rains, we will stay at home.
mistakes.note: After if we use the Present Simple, not will.

forms: If + Past Simple, would + verb
If I were you ... - advice
could or might instead of would

examples.text: If I had more money, I would travel.
If I were you, I would apply.
What would you do if you won the lottery?

mistakes.wrong: If I would have money, I would buy it.
mistakes.right: If I had money, I would buy it.
mistakes.note: The if-part uses the Past Simple, without would.

forms: to be + V3: is cleaned, was cleaned
by + the doer (if it is important)
Question: Was it made in China?

examples.text: English is spoken all over the world.
The book was written by Orwell.

mistakes.right: The room is cleaned every day.
mistakes.note: The passive always needs the verb to be.

forms: used to + verb - a past habit
Negative and question: did + use to
would - only for repeated actions

examples.text: I used to play the piano.

mistakes.wrong: I didn't used to like it.
mistakes.right: I didn't use to like it.
mistakes.note: After did the form is use, without -d.

forms: who - people, which - things, that - both
whose - belonging, where - place
You cannot leave out the subject, but you can leave out the object

examples.text: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
The book (that) I bought is great.
This is the town where I was born.

mistakes.wrong: The man which lives next door is a doctor.
mistakes.right: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
mistakes.note: For people we say who.

forms: The tense moves back: is becomes was, will becomes would
Words change: today becomes that day, tomorrow becomes the next day
Questions keep statement word order: He asked where I lived

examples.text: He asked if I was ready.

mistakes.wrong: He asked where did I live.
mistakes.note: A reported question has the word order of a statement.

forms: must be - almost certain
might / may / could be - possible
can't be - impossible
Past: must have + V3

mistakes.note: We do not use to after must.

forms: Gerund: enjoy, finish, mind, avoid + -ing
Infinitive: want, decide, hope, plan + to
After a preposition, always the gerund

examples.text: She is interested in learning Italian.

mistakes.note: After enjoy we need the gerund.

forms: because - reason, so - result
but, although, however - contrast
despite + a noun or a gerund

examples.text: I was tired, so I went to bed.
Although it was cold, we went out.
It was cold. However, we went out.

mistakes.wrong: Despite it was cold, we went out.
mistakes.right: Despite the cold, we went out.
mistakes.note: After despite comes a noun, not a full clause.

forms: have / has been + -ing
Stresses the process and how long it lasts
Result: Present Perfect; process: Continuous

examples.text: I have been working here for five years.
She has been crying - her eyes are red.
How long have you been waiting?

mistakes.wrong: I have been knowing him for years.
mistakes.right: I have known him for years.
mistakes.note: With state verbs we use the Present Perfect.

forms: had + V3
An action that happened before another action in the past
Time words: after, before, by the time, already, just

examples.text: When I arrived, the film had already started.
She told me she had lost her bag.
By the time we got there, they had left.

mistakes.wrong: When I arrived, the film already started.
mistakes.right: When I arrived, the film had already started.
mistakes.note: The earlier action is in the Past Perfect.

forms: will be + -ing - in progress at a moment in the future
will have + V3 - finished by a moment
will have been + -ing - how long, up to a moment

examples.text: This time tomorrow I will be flying to Rome.
By June I will have finished my degree.
By May we will have been living here for ten years.

mistakes.wrong: By June I will finish my degree.
mistakes.right: By June I will have finished my degree.
mistakes.note: "Finished by a certain moment" needs the Future Perfect.

forms: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3
Mixed: If + Past Perfect, would + verb (result now)
could have, might have instead of would have

examples.text: If I had studied, I would have passed.
If I had taken that job, I would be rich now.
She wouldn't have missed the bus if she had left earlier.

mistakes.wrong: If I would have known, I would have come.
mistakes.right: If I had known, I would have come.
mistakes.note: We do not use would in the if-part.

forms: wish + Past Simple - about the present
wish + Past Perfect - about the past
wish + would - annoyance at someone's behaviour

examples.text: I wish I had more time.
I wish I had gone to the party.
I wish you would stop shouting.

mistakes.wrong: I wish I will be there.
mistakes.right: I wish I could be there.
mistakes.note: We do not use a future tense after wish.

forms: In all tenses: is being built, has been built, will be built
With modal verbs: must be finished
Impersonal: It is said that ... / He is said to be ...
have something done

examples.text: He is said to be rich.

mistakes.right: The report must be finished today.
mistakes.note: After a modal verb we need be + V3.

forms: Yes/no question: asked if / whether
Request and order: told / asked + to
Reporting verbs: suggest, admit, deny, promise, warn, refuse

examples.text: She asked if I was ready.
They suggested going to the cinema.

mistakes.note: After suggest we use the gerund.

forms: Non-defining: between commas, no that
which - refers to the whole sentence
Participle clauses: The man standing there ... (who is standing)

examples.text: My brother, who lives in Berlin, is a teacher.
He passed the exam, which surprised everyone.
The book written by Orwell is famous.

mistakes.wrong: My brother, that lives in Berlin, is a teacher.
mistakes.right: My brother, who lives in Berlin, is a teacher.
mistakes.note: We do not use that in non-defining clauses.

forms: should have + V3 - it was the right thing to do
could have + V3 - it was possible
must have + V3 - almost certainly
can't have + V3 - it was impossible

examples.text: He must have missed the bus.

mistakes.note: After should we need have + V3.

forms: stop doing - end it; stop to do - stop in order to
remember doing - a memory; remember to do - do not forget
try doing - test it; try to do - make an effort

mistakes.right: I forgot to lock the door.
mistakes.note: To say you did not do something, use forget + to + infinitive.

forms: verb + particle: give up, look after
Separable: put on the jacket / put it on
Inseparable: look after them

mistakes.note: A pronoun goes between the verb and the particle.

forms: Contrast: whereas, nevertheless, on the contrary
Adding: moreover, furthermore, besides
Result: therefore, consequently, as a result

examples.text: The plan was risky. Nevertheless, they went ahead.
He was ill; therefore, he stayed home.

mistakes.wrong: Nevertheless of the rain, we went out.
mistakes.right: Despite the rain, we went out.
mistakes.note: Nevertheless is an adverb, not a preposition.
